Armed Conflict & Security
• Israeli strikes hit Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, killing at least six including a surgeon, as Israel says it targeted Hamas militants; health groups warn Gaza’s medical system is collapsing under attacks and detentions.
• Russia’s continued attacks on Ukraine’s power grid have left communities facing prolonged blackouts; a major Ukrainian power plant remains under constant drone and missile threat while Kyiv says it struck Russia’s largest Siberian oil refinery again.
• At least five people were shot in Washington, DC’s Logan Circle area, prompting a shelter-in-place order amid an active police response.
• Italy reported over 1,800 hoax bomb alerts targeting schools, underscoring Europe’s concern over hybrid threats; UK military partners with astronomers to track foreign spy satellites via ground telescopes.
Why it matters: Civilian infrastructure and healthcare are increasingly in the crosshairs of modern conflicts, raising humanitarian stakes and regional risks even as hybrid and domestic security threats test resilience at home.

She said she was concerned by the idea that the cuts would apply to people already getting sickness and disability benefits, and she said it appeared to be a breach of a promise given last year that people already getting Pip (the personal independence payment) would not lose it.She said:I just don’t think that you get a disabled young person into work by taking away the money that helps them to get into work.The cuts seem to land on young disabled people, and many of them are in college already or already in work. So I don’t see how you fix the first by punishing the second.Milburn said he concluded fundamental change was needed. He said:The whole system needs to be changed, because the system is geared to keeping people inactive when, for young people in particular, it’s all about how can you make them active, get them earning, learning, so that they can rely on a wage rather than on a benefit. So, this is not about cutting one benefit, it’s about rebuilding the system from scratch.He said that he decided existing claimants should be covered by the changes, not just new changes.It’s a big rewriting of the welfare system. And obviously one of the conundrums was, ‘Should this apply to only new claimants?’I came to the conclusion that wouldn’t be right, not least because you’ve got hundreds of thousands of young people stuck in a benefit system that is trapping them in poverty, giving them no prospect of prosperity or a job.Milburn admitted this meant the plans would not be “pain-free”.I’m not saying that any of this will be easy or that it will be pain-free because it won’t. You know, candidly, it could mean that some people will get less financial support at the beginning of their benefit claim than under the current system.He said he wanted the system to prioritise improving people’s life chances in the long term over easing their financial hardship in the short term.Actually for young people there’s a different debate that we’ve got to resolve, which is whether the priority is their longer-term life chances or just their immediate shorter-term finances.I think what the current system does, it prioritises the latter over the former. I believe that’s the wrong choice and it needs to be the other way around.He said, alongside the cuts to benefits he is proposing (see 11.56am), he wanted to improve employment support for young people.We need to make sure people have the opportunities to get an apprenticeship, a job, a work placement, a pre-apprenticeship, a college place.The menu of opportunities has got to increase. They’ll have a personal adviser, they’ll be coached all the way through. The adviser will stick with them until they have found a job or an apprenticeship or college place.He also confirmed he wants to let young people do some work before they start losing benefits.They will get immediate access to support if that’s what they need, if that’s the thing that is holding them back from being in education or training.He admitted that offering better employment support and mental health support would mean his plans would initially cost money. According to the Times, he did not did not deny claims the whole package could cost £6bn. But, in the long run, there would be savings, he said.Obviously this costs money. And frankly it’s a better use of money, both from the point of view of the young person and the taxpayer, to spend that money getting them into work rather than spending that money keeping them on benefits.This is the sort of fatuous thing about this debate. You’ve got to invest upfront in order to get savings out of the back end. Cost-free is fatuous. So we’ve got to be candid about that. It will need significant investment.To get a return on investment will take time … the only way of cutting the benefits bill sustainably is by getting young people into work, paying their taxes and being less reliant on benefits. Unless you are prepared to put the investment upfront it will never be possible.He said he was “confident” that Andy Burnham was full-square behind the changes that are needed.” Continue reading...

Economy & Markets.title: Jensen Huang Resigns From Nvidia
Economy & Markets.text: SummaryNvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned on Thursday following revelations of two extramarital affairsThe board weighed Huang's fate over relationships with an alleged Chinese spy and Nvidia vice president Kimberly PowellWith CFO Colette Kress tapped for an interim takeover plan, Nvidia shares dropped over 11 percent in premarket tradingNvidia co-founder and chief executive officer Jensen Huang has resigned from his leadership role on Thursday, according to the Silicon Valley chip giant’s board of directors. Capping a swift fall for one of the central figures in the artificial intelligence boom, the departure follows a multi-hour board meeting on Wednesday convened to weigh Huang’s fate amid revelations of two extramarital affairs.According to the reports, Huang admitted to an extramarital relationship with a woman whom U.S. intelligence agencies concluded was spying for China. Separately, five anonymous former Nvidia employees revealed that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care—an executive who reported directly to him, running counter to the company’s code of conduct barring personal relationships that create workplace conflicts of interest.Although Huang fought to retain his position at the company he founded, an interim plan for Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to take over Nvidia was already well underway. Unwinding Huang’s unconventional, flat management structure—which bypassed traditional organizational charts in favor of more than 60 direct reports, project-focused meetings across all levels, and thousands of daily emails—could complicate a leadership transition. Meanwhile, Nvidia shares plunged more than 11% in premarket trading Thursday, sending tremors through global markets and extending a decline set to wipe roughly $1 trillion from the company’s market value this month alone.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Sports.title: norda’s Trail Team Capsule Puts Its Elite Athletes’ Hardrock Miles to Work
Sports.text: Summarynorda debuts its Trail Team capsule, featuring piecesbuilt from grueling ultra-marathon testing.The range highlights the brand's first hydration vest, Smoky Quartz 055 runners, Luster Cap and Podium Shirt.Launching globally on November 12, priced between $85 and $325 USD.norda is releasing its new Trail Team capsule, a four-piece collection shaped by the brand’s roster of elite trail runners. The pieces are built on years of feedback and real-world miles from athletes who train and race at the top of the sport. The capsule includes norda’s first-ever hydration vest, the Aura 12L, a limited Smoky Quartz version of its 055 racing shoe, and two team-inspired apparel pieces, the Luster Cap and the Podium Shirt.The Aura 12L is the centerpiece, an ultralight vest built for the long efforts of races like UTMB and the Hardrock 100. It has nine pockets for food and gear, anchors for a pole quiver and reflective accents for low light, and it uses a mix of elastic and open mesh to stay comfortable and stable on the move. Trail Team athlete Jimmy Elam tested the vest in the San Juan Mountains and through Hardrock itself, a 100-mile Colorado race known for its punishing altitude. “The vest feels like an extension of my body, with moments I forget I’m wearing it at all,” Elam said in a press release, adding that it has held up just as well since the race.The rest of the capsule balances race performance with team identity. The 055, norda’s top-tier all-terrain racing shoe built for speed and support over long distances, comes in a limited Smoky Quartz colorway with a deliberately minimal look. The Luster Cap is made in Canada from a mono dobby nylon whose sheen changes tone as the light shifts, and its Trail Team details add visibility as the sun goes down. The Podium Shirt has a boxy cut in premium cotton and is pattern-developed and made in Los Angeles. It features a mounted collar, single-stitch construction and a subtle woven label, and its prints are applied by hand so each piece comes out slightly different.The Trail Team capsule launches globally today, November 12, at 6 AM ET, in stores and online at nordarun.com with prices ranging from $85 - $325 USD.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Behind the Doors of Dolomite’s ICONICA Launch Event
Entertainment.text: Dolomite, the heritage mountaineering brand, took over Antonia Milano last week with a special event celebrating the launch of its ICONICA footwear collection. Landing on the brand’s 130th anniversary, the technical range offers a refined expression of its DNA – from alpine landscapes to now contemporary settings across the globe. Comprising a low-cut model, high version and a women's silhouette, ICONICA models come wrapped in fine wax suede leather, crafted to adopt scratches over their lifetime of wear, while details like visible stitching, contrasting panels and metal hardware lean into its forward-thinking design approach. At the recent event, Hypebeast caught up with Dolomite’s head of creative and innovation, Enrico Pizzolato, to find out more about the collection. He shared, “For the 130th anniversary of the brand, we looked closely at our heritage. With mountain boots and technical gear, Dolomite’s archive is dictated by Montebelluna, the heart of the sport system district, and that’s where we drew most of our inspiration from.”“In essence, the design is simple; we didn't want to overcomplicate it and paid close attention to the materials,” he added. “The leather is from Tuscany, and the sole is Vibram®, a brand that’s been our partner for 70 years now. We wanted all these components to be from Italy because the production has always been based here, just ten kilometres from the head office. There are elements of the old shoes here, but the colors and finishes look ahead.”Spotlighting both tradition and innovation, the shoes were placed in a sleek window display facing the Portrait Milano courtyard, where luxury boutiques and designer shops are located. Inside, the futuristic steel shelving was stacked with alternating colorways of “Bone White,” “Goat Beige,” and “Mustard Yellow,” inviting guests to pick them up and take a closer look. Elsewhere, DJ Lemme took to the decks to spin tracks throughout the night. As the Dolomite team joined local tastemakers, models and stylists, they enjoyed a tailored cocktail menu, with the fruity Arctic Blush and sharp 1987 reinterpreting the brand’s longstanding outdoor spirit. After chatting about footwear, heritage and style at the event, Dolomite’s head of marketing, Cristina Bonora, shared her joy in being able to celebrate the brand’s story. She said, “We are defined by passion, craftsmanship and constant evolution. With ICONICA, we wanted to capture that heritage in a collection that looks to the future while staying genuinely connected to our roots and to Made in Italy. We are especially pleased to begin these celebrations with Antonia, which shares our commitment to quality, design and creative exploration.”Be sure to take a look back at the event in the gallery above. Dolomite ICONICA collection is now available to buy on its website and in select retail stores, including Antonia Milano.Read more at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: RIMOWA and Maison Margiela Unveil Limited-Edition Bianchetto Travel Collection
Entertainment.text: SummaryRIMOWA and Maison Margiela have unveiled a limited-edition travel set featuring the Classic Cabin suitcase and 5AC XL bagBoth pieces are finished with hand-painted Bianchetto white paint that cracks and forms a unique patina with wearThe collaborative collection releases on November 19 at select stores and online priced at €3200 and €3600German luggage purveyor RIMOWA and French luxury fashion house Maison Margiela have partnered on a limited-edition travel collection, introducing a collaborative Classic Cabin suitcase and 5AC XL bag. Uniting both houses' design codes, the two-piece travel set explores the beauty of lived experience through hand-painted treatments and seamless structural details.Central to the collaboration is Maison Margiela’s archival Bianchetto technique, where white paint is hand-applied across both the anodized aluminum suitcase and leather bag. Designed to gradually crack, chip, and flake with regular travel, the treatment develops an evolving patina alongside RIMOWA's aviation-inspired grooved surface. The Classic Cabin, manufactured at RIMOWA's Cologne factory, incorporates an inside-out white lining with visible stitching and overlocked edges, an aluminum logo badge secured with four white stitches, a stage-free telescopic handle, TSA-approved locks, and a Multiwheel system.Mirroring the luggage, the 5AC XL bag translates RIMOWA's signature grooves directly into leather using a seamless high-frequency technique. Built with an exposed lining, a leather crossbody strap, and removable loops that attach atop the suitcase's handle, the bag aligns with the suitcase grooves into a unified set. A bespoke leather tag combining RIMOWA’s address tag and Margiela's key bell finishes both pieces.The RIMOWA x Maison Margiela Classic Cabin and 5AC XL Bag will be available starting November 19, 2026, at RIMOWA and Maison Margiela.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Ulysse Nardin Closes the Titanium Freak [S] Chapter With a Purple Enamel Finale
Entertainment.text: SummaryUlysse Nardin marks 25 years of the Freak with the 50-piece Freak [S Purple Enamel].The timepiece spotlights a rotating purple guilloché-flinqué enamel hour disc crafted by Donzé Cadrans.Priced at $174,400 USD, the timepiece is driven by the dual-oscillator Calibre UN-251 with 72 hours of power reserve.Ulysse Nardin is marking two milestones in 2026: 180 years since its founding in Le Locle and 25 years since the debut of the Freak. Launched in 2001 and designed by Dr. Ludwig Oechslin, the original Freak broke every convention with no dial, no hands and no crown and a movement that rotated to tell the time, while also being the first watch to use silicon components.The latest chapter is the Freak [S Purple Enamel], the final titanium Freak [S] with an enamel hour disc. Two oversized silicon balance wheels, each tilted at 20 degrees and fitted with DIAMonSIL escapements, are linked by a 47-part vertical differential on ceramic ball bearings, which the brand calls the smallest of its kind in the world, averaging their rates for greater accuracy. The mechanism spreads across six gear planes instead of the usual two, and about 95% of its parts are in motion at any time. The patented Grinder winding system keeps everything running for 72 hours.True to the Freak's rules, the wearer sets the time by unlocking a latch at 6 o'clock and turning the bezel, and winds it by flipping the watch over and turning the caseback. Each piece is assembled start to finish by a single Grandes Complications watchmaker. The purple hour disc is the edition's standout feature. It was made in-house at Donzé Cadrans, the Swiss enamel workshop that Ulysse Nardin acquired in 2011. Unlike a static dial, this disc rotates as part of the movement, so it is built on an 18-carat white gold base chosen for its stability under repeated kiln firings. The disc is stamped with an in-house guilloché-style pattern, then coated in hand-ground enamel over three to four layers, each fired at around 800°C, and finally polished by hand for about an hour.The 45mm case, bezel, locking mechanism and caseback are all titanium, measuring 16.65mm tall overall, with 30 meters of water resistance and a purple calfskin strap with white stitching and a titanium folding buckle. Limited to 50 examples, the Freak [S Purple Enamel] will be available via the brand at a retail price point ot $174,400 USD. For more information, head over to Ulysse Nardin's official website.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Netflix’s ‘The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez’ Finally Unseals Pac’s Unaired 1996 Interview
Entertainment.text: SummaryAngie Martinez is releasing never-before-heard portions of a Tupac Shakur interview she recorded at his Los Angeles home months before his deathThe four-episode video podcast pairs the original audio with reflections from 15 guests who lived through the era or helped shape how it’s rememberedMartinez withheld the most inflammatory parts for nearly three decades out of concern they could inflame an already dangerous climateNetflix is set to premiere The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez, a four-episode video podcast built around previously unreleased material from Martinez’s 1996 sit-down with Tupac Shakur. The Radio Hall of Famer and New York Times bestselling author recorded the conversation early in her New York radio career, aired only select portions at the time and kept the rest private for close to 30 years.The interview itself came together through an unlikely detour. Tupac first contacted Martinez hoping she would appear in his “I Ain’t Mad at Cha” music video, a request she turned down given the tension surrounding him in New York at the time. Their conversation shifted when he made clear his grievances weren’t aimed at the entire city, a point Martinez felt the public needed to hear directly from him, so he invited her to Los Angeles to record at his home, where he greeted her with New York pizza to make her feel welcome.Back at the station, Martinez made the editorial call that defines the series. She broadcast the sections that conveyed Tupac’s core message that he wasn’t feuding with a whole coast, then physically sliced out the more volatile remarks with a razor blade, worried they could hurt people, fracture relationships or escalate an already deadly situation. His death months later only complicated the choice further, as she felt responsible for protecting words that were never intended to be his last public statement. Martinez was also on air the day he died, delivering the news to her listeners herself.Her reasoning for releasing the tapes now centers on legacy and context. “They’re a piece of hip-hop history, and I don’t think they should just sit in my possession forever,” Martinez told Netflix Tudum. Rather than serve up the most explosive clips for reaction, the four-part structure gives her space to run two parallel narratives: the collision of hip-hop, media and the wider world in 1996, and her own story as a young woman in radio suddenly holding information with real consequences.Fleshing out those perspectives is a deliberately varied guest roster featuring Matt Barnes, Big Boy, Bootleg Kev, Joe Budden, Charlamagne Tha God, DJ Hed, E.D.I. Mean, Erica Ford, Dream Hampton, Lil’ Cease, Monie Love, Ed Lover, Aiyisha T. Obafemi, Wallo and RZA. Martinez says she avoided booking a panel that would simply agree with one another or rehash familiar anecdotes, instead seeking out people who were present, who knew Tupac in different ways, or who could push back on how the period is remembered.Behind the scenes, Martinez serves as executive producer alongside Brittany Ortiz, Matt Barnes, Brian Dailey, Stephen Jackson, Jelani McCoy and Christina Mizzi, with IRL Productions and All the Smoke Productions handling production. All the Smoke shares its name with the podcast co-hosted by former NBA players Barnes and Jackson.Revisiting the recordings now, Martinez says what stands out most is how young Tupac was, just 25 when he died, and how much hurt and frustration sat beneath his anger. She acknowledges he says things she disagrees with, but frames the project as an attempt to restore the person behind the symbol. “Not as a saint, not as a villain, but as a brilliant, flawed, deeply human young man whose life and work still have so much to teach us,” she told Tudum.The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez premieres November 27 on Netflix.Read more at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: A Remix of Kendrick Lamar’s “The Blacker the Berry” Soundtracks a Gunfight in Netflix’s ‘Bass X Machina’
Entertainment.text: SummaryKendrick Lamar’s “The Blacker the Berry” soundtracks a gunfight in an episode of the new Netflix anime Bass X Machina Brian Tyree Henry stars as Bass Reeves, whose mid-reload warning to his enemies kicks off the trackThe song arrives as a remix reworked to blend into the episode’s sound designNetflix’s Bass X Machina has pulled Kendrick Lamar’s “The Blacker the Berry” into one of its fiercest set pieces, a close-quarters gunfight staged inside a moving train. The 2015 To Pimp a Butterfly remix track arrives at the exact moment the scene tips from tense standoff into full-blown firefight, turning a Netflix action beat into a Kendrick moment.Everything hinges on a single line from Brian Tyree Henry’s Bass Reeves. Surrounded and outgunned, the lawman calmly tells his attackers they have only as long as it takes him to load his weapon to change their minds, and when nobody takes the offer, Kendrick’s opening bars hit. The version heard on screen isn’t a straight needle drop either, as the song has been reshaped to mesh with the episode’s gunshots, rattling train cars and score.The pairing carries extra weight given who the show is built around. The real Bass Reeves, born into slavery, became one of the first Black deputy US marshals west of the Mississippi River and is often cited as a possible inspiration for the Lone Ranger. Setting his on-screen showdown to a record so focused on Black identity and defiance makes the choice feel deliberate rather than decorative.Catch the “The Blacker the Berry” sequence in Bass X Machina, streaming now on Netflix.🚨kendrick remix in bass x machina alert 🚨 https://t.co/oWmrn0OKre— Strong Black Lead (@strongblacklead) November 7, 2026Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
